0.comment: Jean: Barbara and the Gunnhildr family
0.content: Jean's parents are Frederica Gunnhildr, the Alder Knight of the Gunnhildr Clan, and Seamus Pegg, a famed adventurer who became the Church of Favonius's Seneschal, the Cardinal of Daybreak. They separated when the girls were small. Jean stayed with her mother, who raised her strictly as heir to the clan, and Barbara went with their father into the Church. Jean has always wanted to be closer to her sister but cannot find the words before Barbara's evasive glances; Barbara is equally awkward, and secretly worries about her. When Jean collapsed from overwork, Barbara nursed her and told her friends that Jean goes to Vennessa's tree when she feels lost, then claimed Jean had "mentioned it".

1.content: Varka, the Knight of Boreas and Grand Master, left six months before the Traveler arrived with the Knights' elite, telling Jean, "you've basically been doing my job for years now, anyway." She once begged him to take his job seriously; he replied that helping him was part of a second-in-command's job. She does not resent him. He is "the knight of new frontiers", she "the knight of maintaining peace and freedom", and she vowed to show him a kinder, more prosperous Mondstadt on his return. She calls him the legend of his generation.

2.content: Jean is one of the few Mondstadters who know the bard Venti is Barbatos; she worked it out on her own. She keeps the secret absolutely, calls him Lord Barbatos only in private, and does not question an Archon's "own calculations". He agrees she is conscientious, courageous, kind and considerate, and says she reminds him of another good friend without saying whom.

3.content: After the Traveler helped drive off Stormterror and stabilise the elemental flow, Jean asked them to accept the title of Honorary Knight "and the gratitude of the Acting Grand Master". She has relied on them ever since, saying they have never failed Mondstadt in its time of need. She has sworn that, "not as the Acting Grand Master, but as Jean", her sword will always go with them.

4.comment: Jean: Diluc and the Eroch affair
4.content: Jean calls Diluc her senior and says they share the same commitment to protecting Mondstadt, though they have gone separate ways. He left the Knights after Inspector Eroch ordered him to cover up the death of his father, Crepus. Jean accepts his criticism ("I am not proud of the way things went, but I cannot change the past") and hopes her work will change his view. Diluc says trifling matters are her greatest enemy and that her sense of responsibility has kept her from her true calling. He still sponsored the party for her, saying he owes her his gratitude like any citizen.

5.comment: Jean: Vennessa, the Dandelion Knight and the Lionfang Knight
5.content: Vennessa founded the Knights of Favonius about a thousand years ago and ended her journey at Windrise, leaving a sapling that became the great tree. Jean reveres her. Jean says Vennessa was the Lionfang Knight when she overthrew the aristocracy and the Dandelion Knight when she founded the Knights, and that Masters of the Knights inherit one title or the other. After her collapse Jean prayed beneath the tree that Vennessa's watch over Mondstadt would remain unclouded, and later decided she is "definitely more of a Dandelion Knight": the Lionfang Knight stands for Vennessa's past battles, the Dandelion Knight for her hopes for the future.

6.comment: Jean: Jean's collapse and the thank-you party
6.content: In her story quest (1.0), the Traveler relays three requests to Jean: Sara's blocked supply road, Charles's tax forms and Margaret's missing cat Prince. Mid-report Jean stops responding and collapses from burnout; Barbara says it is not the first time. While she recovers, the Traveler takes over her commissions. She slips out to Windrise, where an Abyss Mage tries to kill her "in her moment of weakness", and despite coughing she insists on pursuing it. Back in the city, Swan lures her to Angel's Share, where the Knights, Barbara, Diluc and a very drunk Venti throw her a thank-you party; they have finished every task on her list. She is left speechless, then thanks everyone and slips up to the balcony.
